inline_comments.comment: This `overrides` entry for `["*.md", "*.mdx"]` is dead configuration. Both patterns also appear in `ignorePatterns` (lines 38–39), so oxfmt never processes those files and the override never fires. Either remove `*.md` / `*.mdx` from `ignorePatterns` and rely on this override to limit what formatting rules apply, or delete the override block. Leaving it creates the false impression that md/mdx formatting is being configured when it is not.

The second glob in this override — `**/frameworks/angular/template/**/*.ts` — matches paths already excluded by `"code/frameworks/angular/template/**"` in `ignorePatterns` (line 33). Files in ignored paths are never passed to oxfmt, so the `babel-ts` parser override is a no-op for those files. Either remove that glob from the override, remove the path from `ignorePatterns`, or add a comment clarifying that the override is forward-looking for when the ignore rule is lifted.

The file is missing a trailing newline (`\ No newline at end of file`). POSIX requires text files to end with a newline; its absence produces noisy one-line diffs and can cause tools that stream the file line-by-line to drop the final line. Ironic given the PR is about enforcing consistent formatting.
Same missing-trailing-newline issue as `extensions.json`. The diff clearly shows `+}\n\ No newline at end of file` for both files.

The original code had `
    …

      ` — a duplicate opening `
        ` tag instead of the closing `
      `. This means the `
        ` is never closed, producing invalid HTML that browsers will attempt to repair heuristically. The reformatting here fixes it to `
          …

        `. This is a genuine functional correction mixed into what is presented as a pure-formatting change. It should be called out explicitly in the PR description so reviewers know to scrutinize it rather than assume the diff is whitespace-only.

`"lint": "yarn lint:js && cd .. && yarn fmt:check"` uses a shell `cd` inside a yarn script. This is bash/zsh-specific and does not work on Windows cmd.exe. More importantly, a `cd` in a `&&` chain mutates working-directory state for the remainder of the shell fragment in a fragile way. Prefer the portable workspace-flag form: `"lint": "yarn lint:js && yarn --cwd .. fmt:check"`.

The previous `code/package.json` lint-staged config invoked `oxfmt` (write/fix mode) on staged files, automatically correcting formatting before the commit landed. The new root config switches to `"oxfmt --check"` (report-only). This is a breaking behavioral change for any contributor who does not have the OXC VS Code extension installed with `formatOnSave: true`: their commits will now be blocked by the pre-commit hook with a formatting error rather than being silently corrected. If the team wants a check-only policy, this should be documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and the OXC extension should be treated as a required setup step rather than a recommendation.

The `scripts/**` pattern in lint-staged only runs ESLint (`yarn --cwd scripts lint:js:cmd`), while the `code/**` patterns also run `oxfmt --check`. Files under `scripts/` will therefore not be format-checked on commit even though the root oxfmt config covers them. If oxfmt should also guard `scripts/` files pre-commit, add `"oxfmt --check"` to this pattern the same way it is added for `code/**`.

general_comments.comment: The root `.oxfmtrc.json` adds `"docs"` to `ignorePatterns`, completely excluding the docs directory from the main `fmt:check`/`fmt:write` sweep. The `scripts/package.json` then re-enters `docs/_snippets` via `cd ../docs && oxfmt --config ./.oxfmtrc.json --check ./_snippets`. This two-level approach is workable but non-obvious: a developer running `yarn fmt:write` from root will silently skip docs snippets. A brief inline comment next to `"docs"` in `ignorePatterns` (e.g., `// formatted separately by scripts/package.json fmt:check`) and a note in CONTRIBUTING.md would prevent confusion.

`lint-staged` is bumped from 16.2.7 to 16.4.0. The new version replaces the `micromatch` glob library with `picomatch` and swaps `nano-spawn`/`pidtree` for `tinyexec`. The root lint-staged config introduces deep `**` patterns (e.g., `code/**/*.{js,jsx,mjs,ts,tsx}`) that were not present in the old per-package configs. `micromatch` and `picomatch` are broadly compatible but diverge subtly on brace expansion edge cases and Windows path separator handling. Verify the new patterns match the intended file sets — in particular that staged files in deeply nested `code/` paths are correctly selected — before relying on this in CI.
